influences.name: John Cale
influences.context: John Cale's Paris 1919 was credited by the band as providing a musical parallel. According to Tweedy, "It was eye-opening that I wasn't the only person that felt like these worlds had a lot more in common than they'd been given credit for—that experimentation and avant-garde theory was not directly opposed to beauty, y'know?"

influences.name: Bob Rock
influences.context: There's a story about someone, Bob Rock or somebody, who just comes in and puts a piece of cardboard over every meter in the entire house. Why do I need these? I'm using my ears.

influences.name: Bob Dylan
influences.context: Are there any songwriters that are still mysterious to you, just in terms of what they are able to produce? Take Bob Dylan — you're a songwriter, you know how songwriting works, but can you still wrap your head around what he does? ... If I think about Bob Dylan, what he does, what he gets out of himself year after year, all I think is he must read and write and think about it a lot more than a lot of other people and he's been able to maintain that energy for a long time. He has protected the part of himself that is inspired, I think, in a way that I find inspiring myself.

influences.name: Woody Guthrie
influences.context: In folk music — the musical tradition that I'm probably closest to — originality is not a primary concern. What the primary concern would be is telling the story effectively and making a connection and relating what you want to relate. Woody Guthrie always claimed that he never wrote an original melody on purpose, and it was only if he misremembered something he was trying to steal. At the same time, I think Woody Guthrie sounds like nobody else and he's an icon of individuality and originality and uniqueness.

influences.name: Inuit carvers
influences.context: Then I read somewhere about how Inuit carvers create. As I understand it, they take a walrus tusk, or a piece of limestone, and they don't think, "I'm going to carve an elk or a seal or an eagle." They simply carve, and as they go, they discover what's inside the walrus tusk they're cutting into. And they believe that was there, that they just opened it up and revealed it. That's what I'm like when I'm in my most ideal state of creativity
